# SocialCrawl API Overview

## Base URL

```
https://www.socialcrawl.dev
```

## Authentication

Pass your API key in the `x-api-key` header with every request:

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/profile?handle=charlidamelio"
```

## Surface

<!-- BEGIN:GENERATED:SURFACE (auto-generated by generate-docs.ts - AIP-16b) -->
**68 platforms, 645 active endpoints** (32 of them social). Most are `GET /v1/{platform}/{resource}`, but not all: the batch read endpoints take a JSON body over POST, and the stateful `/v1/web/*` job, monitor, and session routes use POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE. Three surfaces sit on top of the registry: the cross-platform **Prism** composites (`/v1/prism/*` and per-platform `profile/full` / `omni-search`), the stateful **Monitors** family (`/v1/monitors/*`), and the stateful **Cohorts** family (`/v1/cohorts/*` + `/v1/cohort-queries/*`) - neither stateful family is counted in the 645. One more call fans out across 17 sources at once: `/v1/search/everywhere`. See [prism.md](prism.md), [monitors.md](monitors.md), [cohorts.md](cohorts.md), and [search.md](search.md).
<!-- END:GENERATED:SURFACE -->

## Response Format

All successful responses follow this envelope:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "platform": "tiktok",
  "endpoint": "/v1/tiktok/profile",
  "data": { ... },
  "credits_used": 1,
  "credits_remaining": 4999,
  "request_id": "req-XXXXX",
  "cached": false
}
```

Every **list** response also carries a top-level `pagination` block alongside `data`:

```json
"pagination": { "next_cursor": "sc.eyJ...", "has_more": true, "page_size": 30 }
```

`has_more` is the explicit stop signal. Prefer it over inspecting `data.next_cursor` (retained for backwards compatibility) or `total` (which can be estimated or absent).

Two optional root keys can also appear: `idempotent_replay: true` on an idempotency replay, and `meta.hint` on the rare response that completed a multi-call pattern one other call does in a single step (see [Chain hints](#chain-hints-metahint)).

**Where things live.** This is the most common integration mistake, so check it before reading a field:

| At the envelope root | Inside `data` |
|---|---|
| `success`, `platform`, `endpoint`, `credits_used`, `credits_remaining`, `request_id`, `cached` | The payload: `author` / `post` / `items[]` / ... |
| `pagination` (`next_cursor`, `has_more`, `page_size`, and `stopped_at` when you sent `since` / `stop_at_id`) | `dropped` (every list), `_warnings` (advisory notices) |
| `meta.hint` (optional) | Page reports: `labels`, `relevance`, `label_share`, `comment_language`, `comment_recency`, `creator_baseline`, `hydration`, `walk`, `scan`, `held_back`, `estimate` |
| `idempotent_replay` (replays only) | Per-row judgments sit on each row under `computed` (`computed.labels`, `computed.relevance`, `computed.vs_creator`) |

`credits_remaining` is `integer | null`. It is authoritative on a **billed** response, where it comes straight from the deduction. Every free response-cache hit deliberately skips a blocking balance read, so its body value is `null` and `X-Credits-Remaining` is omitted. An idempotency replay also uses that unknown representation if its current-balance lookup fails. **`null` means unknown; it is never a fabricated zero**, so a `0` here really does mean the account is empty. Poll `GET /v1/credits/balance` when you need a guaranteed reading, and gate any pause-or-alert logic on `!== null && === 0` rather than on falsiness.

Error responses:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS",
    "message": "Your account has 0 credits remaining. This endpoint requires 1 credits. Retrying this request will not succeed until your account balance changes.",
    "status": 402,
    "doc_url": "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/docs/errors#insufficient-credits",
    "retryable": false,
    "details": {
      "reason": "balance_too_low",
      "retry_will_succeed": false,
      "next_step": "Top up your credits on the billing page ...",
      "top_up_url": "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/dashboard/billing/payments",
      "credits_required": 1
    }
  },
  "credits_used": 0,
  "credits_remaining": 0,
  "request_id": "req-XXXXX"
}
```

`error.retryable` is on every error and is derived from the status (429, 500, 502, 503, 504 are retryable; everything else is not). `error.details` is present only when there is structured context to act on; branch on `error.details.reason` when it is there. The reasons are listed under [Error details](#error-details-errordetails).

## Response Headers

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| X-Request-Id | Unique request identifier (`req-XXXXX`) |
| X-Credits-Used | Credits consumed by this request (`0` on cache hit, idempotent replay, empty list, or refunded error) |
| X-Credits-Remaining | Balance after deduction. Omitted when the balance is unknown (free cache hits) |
| X-Cache | `HIT` or `MISS` |
| X-Idempotent-Replay | `"true"` when the request was served as an idempotent replay. Absent otherwise. |
| X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset | Request-window budget (600/min per key). `-Reset` omitted when the limiter is degraded |
| X-Concurrency-Limit / -Remaining | Concurrency headroom (50 per key) as this request entered |
| Retry-After | Seconds to wait, on 503 circuit-breaker (`"30"`), 429 `RATE_LIMITED` / `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT`, 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` (`"1"`), and a repeat 402 from an out-of-credits key (`"60"`). A source that is known to be unavailable for a market can send a long value (for example `"3600"`) |
| Allow | The method(s) the endpoint actually accepts, only on 405 `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` responses. Not always `GET`: the batch and `/v1/web/*` routes accept POST/PATCH/DELETE |

## Request Controls That Work Across Endpoints

These are not per-platform parameters. Each one is accepted wherever its column says, and none of them is billed on its own.

| Control | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `format=raw` | Normalized endpoints | Returns the upstream body verbatim. See [Raw Format](#raw-format) |
| `fields=<paths>` | Every GET endpoint, and `?fields=` on the POST batch reads | Returns only the fields you name on each row (plus `id` / `url`). Cuts tokens, not credits. See [Field Projection](#field-projection) |
| `judgments=off` (or `label=none`) | Every endpoint that carries default labels or relevance | Turns the free default judgments off: the page is exactly what it was before judgments existed |
| `dry_run=1` | Every endpoint | On servers where `/v1/utility/estimate` exists (a 404 there means an older server that honours `dry_run=1` only on labelled endpoints and bills it elsewhere), a free preview: validates the request and returns `data.valid`, `data.normalized_params` and `data.estimate` (the quote for the real call, plus the label / relevance credits on labelled endpoints). Fetches nothing, 0 credits |
| `fit=goal&goal=<your task>` | Labelled and relevance endpoints | Trims the page to the rows and fields needed for that goal; the rest are stubbed and listed in `data.held_back`. Free |
| `Cache-Control: no-cache` header | Every cached GET | Skips the cache lookup (a live, billed fetch) and writes the fresh result back |
| `Idempotency-Key` header | Every charging `/v1/*` call | Makes a retry safe. See [Idempotent Retries](#idempotent-retries) |
| `X-SocialCrawl-Hints: off` header | Every GET | Never receive `meta.hint` |
| `Accept: text/event-stream` header | Streaming endpoints only | Server-Sent Events instead of one JSON body |

## Credit System

<!-- BEGIN:GENERATED:CREDIT_TIERS (auto-generated by generate-docs.ts - AIP-16b) -->
| Tier | Cost | Endpoints | Typical endpoints |
|------|------|-----------|-------------------|
| standard | 1 credit | 244 | Profiles, posts, search, comments, reference data |
| advanced | 5 credits | 166 | Ad libraries, trending, audience analytics, app/product/place reviews, retail catalogs, Google + Naver trends, LinkedIn social graph + jobs, Instagram relationship/discovery data |
| premium | 10 credits | 25 | Video transcripts, LinkedIn people/job search + reactions, app-listings search, web agent jobs |
| **custom (flat / metered)** | **varies (0-10000)** | 210 | `/v1/search/everywhere` (20), `search/forums` (10) & `search/news` (2-62 metered); `naver/brief` (10); `{platform}/profile/full` (5); the free `/v1/utility/*` self-discovery endpoints (0); web scrape/crawl/sessions; all `/v1/prism/*` composites (0-1605, flat or metered per recipe) |

Two groupings, both totalling 645: the table above counts endpoints **by pricing rule** (a custom override is its own row); counted instead **by base tier** (custom endpoints folded back into the ladder tier they sit on) the split is **359 standard · 240 advanced · 46 premium = 645**. Per-endpoint costs, cache TTLs, and the full rule behind every metered endpoint: see [pricing.md](pricing.md).
<!-- END:GENERATED:CREDIT_TIERS -->

Every account starts with **100 free credits**. Credit packs (one-time, no subscription): Starter 2,500 (£15), Growth 20,000 (£49), Pro 150,000 (£299), Enterprise custom. Current packs at https://socialcrawl.dev/pricing.

**Auto-refunds.** Credits are refunded automatically on `502`/`504 UPSTREAM_ERROR`, `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and on the empty-upstream guard: a single-object lookup that finds nothing is `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, and a **list with zero matches is `200` with `items: []` at 0 credits** (it is an answer, not an error). Cache hits, idempotent replays, and 400/405/409/413/422 rejections never deduct at all. You only pay for calls that return real data.

**Holds and settlement.** Metered endpoints, opt-in labels, row hydration and multi-page walks deduct an upfront ceiling and refund down to the work actually done. `credits_used` on the response is always the real charge; a 402 on such a call quotes the ceiling, not the price (`error.details.pricing: "ceiling"`).

## Credit Balance

Check remaining credits via the public, API-key-authed meta endpoint (costs **0 credits**, never cached):

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/credits/balance"
```

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "platform": "meta",
  "endpoint": "/v1/credits/balance",
  "data": {
    "balance": 8432,
    "recent_deductions": { "last_24h": 128, "last_7d": 1043 }
  },
  "credits_used": 0,
  "credits_remaining": 8432,
  "request_id": "req-XXXXX",
  "cached": false
}
```

The dashboard UI uses a separate session-authed `/api/credits/balance` route. Programmatic callers must use `/v1/credits/balance`.

For a full credit ledger (dispute-grade receipts. Deductions negative, refunds positive, newest first), call `GET /v1/credits/transactions` (also **0 credits**, never cached). It is cursor-paginated (`limit` defaults to 50, capped at 100) and filterable by `request_id`:

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/credits/transactions?limit=50"
```

## Unified Canonical Schemas

Author, Post, and Comment endpoints are normalized through per-platform field maps into one canonical shape, validated at the wire, the same JSON structure whether the data came from TikTok, Reddit, or Bluesky.

**Author** (`data.author`): `id`, `username`, `display_name`, `avatar_url`, `bio`, `verified`, `followers`, `following`, `posts_count`, `likes_count`, `url`, `location`, `external_url`. IDs are bare and prefix-stripped (Bluesky `did:`, Spotify `spotify:artist:`, Reddit `t2_` all stripped).

**Post** (`data.post`, or `data.items[].post` in lists): `id`, `url`, `content.{text, media_urls, thumbnail_url, duration_seconds}`, `author.{username, display_name, avatar_url, verified}`, `engagement.{views, likes, comments, shares, saves}`, `flags.{nsfw, spoiler, pinned, deleted}`, `published_at`. `media_urls` is an array for carousels. `flags.deleted` is always present.

**Comment** (`data.comment`, or `data.items[].comment` in lists): `id`, `url`, `parent_id`, `post_id`, `text`, `author.{username, display_name, avatar_url, verified}`, `engagement.{likes, replies}`, `flags.{pinned, deleted}`, `published_at`. Deleted/removed sentinels (`[deleted]`, `[removed]`) never reach `text`/`author`. They become `null` and `flags.deleted` flips `true`.

Platform-specific data that has no canonical field lives in a typed, optional `ext` object on the row (`post.ext`, `author.ext`, `comment.ext`, `product.ext`, `review.ext`). Each platform reference names its `ext` leaves.

**Post and Comment are different archetypes, deliberately.** A post's body is `post.content.text` and its reply count is `post.engagement.comments`; a comment's body is `comment.text` and its reply count is `comment.engagement.replies`. So `/v1/twitter/search/tweets` returns `post.content.text` while `/v1/twitter/tweet/replies` returns `comment.text`, on the same platform, by design: a comment has no media block, no thumbnail and no duration, so it does not carry a `content` wrapper, and "comments on a post" and "replies to a comment" are different quantities that must not share a name. The archetype is named on every endpoint's `**Response**` line, so read that rather than assuming one shape per platform. The search endpoints (`/v1/search/*`) are a third thing again: their `top_comments[]` rows are a search-enrichment structure (`{ score, excerpt, truncated, author, url, date }`), not the Comment archetype, and their body field is `excerpt`.

**Commerce, places & apps archetypes** (the commerce, review, place and app-store platforms):

- **Product**: Amazon, Walmart, Target, eBay, Home Depot, Google Shopping (title, price, rating, brand, images, specifications, variant ids). One shape across all six, so a cross-retailer comparison needs no per-retailer mapping.
- **Review**: shared across Amazon, Walmart, Target, Home Depot, Google Shopping, Trustpilot, Tripadvisor, Google Business, Google Play, Apple App Store (`id`, `title`, `text`, `author`, `rating`, `helpful_votes`, `published_at`, `source`, `responses[]` for owner/developer replies, `images`).
- **Seller**: Amazon, Walmart, Google Shopping per-seller offers (name, price, condition, rating).
- **Place**: Tripadvisor, Google Business (name, category, rating, reviews_count, price_level, phone, latitude/longitude, image_urls; Google hotel results add a `place.hotel` block with amenities, sentiment topics, and multi-vendor prices).
- **App**: Google Play + Apple App Store share one App object with a `store` discriminator (`"google_play"` / `"app_store"`); store-exclusive fields (`installs`/`genres` on Google, `languages`/`advisories` on Apple) are null on the other store.
- **Job**: the LinkedIn job family (listing, detail, search).
- **Quote**: Google Finance instruments and market movers.
- **NewsArticle**: Google News and the news half of universal search.
- **WebPage**: the `/v1/web/*` scrape / crawl / map / extract surface.
- **Audience** / **Analytics** / **Transcript**: audience breakdowns, composite reports, and caption tracks.

Every endpoint section in a platform reference names its archetype on its `**Response**` line.

List endpoints return `{ items: [...], next_cursor?, total? }` regardless of the upstream's original key names. Commerce/place/app list items carry no `computed` block.

Research/analytics endpoints (Tavily, Perplexity, Polymarket, Content Analysis aggregates, twitter ai-search) are passthrough. They keep their upstream's native top-level keys.

## Computed Fields

When a field map applies (the Author/Post endpoints, which is most of the social surface), four derived signals are added under `data.computed`:

| Field | Type | Author formula | Post formula |
|-------|------|---------------|-------------|
| `engagement_rate` | `number \| null` | `likes_count / followers` (clamped `[0, 1]`) | `(likes + comments + shares) / views` (clamped `[0, 1]`) |
| `language` | `string \| null` | ISO 639-1 detected from `bio` | ISO 639-1 detected from `post.content.text` |
| `content_category` | `string` | Keyword-based (15 categories) | Keyword-based (15 categories) |
| `estimated_reach` | `number \| null` | `round(followers * engagement_rate * 0.1)` | `round(views * 1.2)` when `views > 0`, else `null` |

`engagement_rate` returns `null` when the divisor or numerator is missing/zero (never `Infinity`, `NaN`, or negatives). Ratios >1.0 are clamped to 1.0 with a `_warnings` entry. Language detection needs ≥10 chars of text, else `null`.

On the endpoints that carry judgments, each row's `computed` block can also hold `labels`, `relevance` and (creator post lists) `vs_creator`. See [Labels, Relevance and Quality](#labels-relevance-and-quality).

## Integrity: `data.dropped` (list responses)

Every list response carries a `data.dropped` integer, the number of upstream
items discarded because they could not be repaired to the endpoint schema. A
clean page carries `"dropped": 0`, which is a **positive assertion that nothing
was lost**, not a default.

```json
"data": { "items": [ ... ], "total": 42, "dropped": 0 }
```

Read it on every page of a drain. It is the only signal that a page came back
short; `items.length` cannot tell a lossy page from a genuinely small one.

**Placement matters, and it is easy to get wrong.** `dropped` sits inside
`data`, next to `items`, while `pagination` sits at the envelope **root**.
Reading `response.dropped` returns `undefined`, which looks exactly like zero to
a naive check and exactly like an outage to a strict one. Read
`response.data.dropped`.

Singular (non-list) responses carry no `dropped` at all. There is no list to
lose rows from, so its absence there is correct and expected.

## Response Warnings (`data._warnings`)

Successful responses may include an optional `data._warnings: string[]` with non-fatal notices. **It lives inside `data`, never at the envelope root**: a check for a top-level `_warnings` always reads nothing. **Advisory only**: do not flip success, gate retries, or treat it as an error. Empty arrays are omitted, so absent means no warnings.

Read it anyway, because several notices tell you your request was not what you think it was:

| Notice (prefix) | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count was ignored; use limit (page size)` | You sent a parameter the endpoint does not declare. The page is unchanged and billed as normal |
| `<param> was ignored: ...` | Any other undeclared parameter, with the reason: `did you mean <declared>?`, `label=<preset>` is the way to ask for that, `relevance=filter&relevant_to=` for a topic, or `has no such parameter` |
| `resolved_to_different_handle: requested @old, returned @new` | A profile lookup or an `include=` join landed on a different handle. On a lookup the account is the same entity (a rename); on a join that was not the same account, the row is left unfilled and not charged |
| `seen_unavailable` / `seen_refund_failed` | The `seen=` memory or its refund was unavailable; the page came back whole at its full price |
| `moments_unavailable` | A transcript `q=` / `moments=` step could not run; the transcript is returned without `data.moments` |
| `creator_partial` / `creator_unavailable` / `country_no_match` | Instagram reels `include=creator` / `country` notices |
| field-map drift, clamped computed values | A row came back degraded but usable |

A `user_id` that is plainly a username on TikTok or Instagram is looked up as `handle`, with a `_warnings` line saying so.

## Parameter Validation

Every request is validated **before any credit is deducted**, so every rejection below is a free `400 INVALID_REQUEST`:

1. **Required params**: every required name must be present and non-empty.
2. **`oneOf` groups**: endpoints like `GET /v1/youtube/channel` accept `channelId` / `handle` / `url`; at least one member must be present. Reference files render these as "At least one of `a` / `b` is required."
3. **Enum values and bounds**: a value one edit away from a valid one gets `Did you mean '<value>'?` in the message.
4. **Unknown parameter names**: a name one edit away from a declared one is a 400 with `Did you mean '<param>'?` and `error.details.suggestions`; a geographic filter (`country`, `exclude_country`, ...) on a list endpoint that cannot apply it is a 400 with `details.reason: "unsupported_geo_filter"`, because silently returning unfiltered rows would be worse. Any other undeclared parameter is dropped, the call proceeds, and `data._warnings` says it was ignored.
5. **Per-platform format validators**: handles, URLs, subreddits, ASINs (10-char alphanumeric), and URL batches are checked against platform-specific rules at the boundary. A single leading `@` is stripped from handles. Garbage is rejected in <100ms with no charge.

A wrong path is `404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`, also free, and names the closest real endpoint (`Did you mean: /v1/instagram/profile/posts?`) when one is known.

## Pagination

List responses use `{ items, next_cursor?, total? }` inside `data`, plus the top-level `pagination` block described above. **Prefer the unified path:** send `pagination.next_cursor` back verbatim as `cursor`, and stop when `has_more` is `false`. The API mints a unified `sc.`-prefixed token (or `sc2.` on a multi-source endpoint, which pins the follow-up page to the provider that served page 1) and translates it into whatever the upstream actually wants.

The native parameter each endpoint uses is still accepted, and is named on that endpoint's `**Paging**` line in its platform reference. **Most list endpoints paginate** (cursor-based for nearly all platforms; offset-based on Naver):

- **Cursor-based**: pass the cursor back verbatim (don't decode or trim it) as `cursor`, or in the platform's own cursor param: `max_cursor` (TikTok), `continuationToken` (YouTube), `next_max_id` (Instagram, Truth Social), `after` (Reddit), `paginationToken`/`cursor` (LinkedIn), `cursor` (most others). Stop on `pagination.has_more: false`.
- **Offset-based** (Naver only): increment `start` yourself (1-indexed, cap 1000) with `display` page size.
- Page size is upstream-decided (10 to 30 items typical). `total` may be exact, estimated, or missing: never use it to decide when to stop.
- A short or empty page is not the end while `has_more` is `true`. An empty page served because every row on it was a repeat costs 0 credits.
- Endpoints that are single-page by design return `has_more: false` and reject an inbound cursor as a free 400.
- A page past a source's hard page cap is a free 400 with `error.details.reason: "page_limit"`, `max_page`, `requested_page` and `narrow_with` (the parameters that reach different rows). See [Error details](#error-details-errordetails).

## Incremental Sync (`since`, `stop_at_id`)

A poll of a creator's feed can stop where the last poll ended, instead of paying to re-walk pages it already holds. Both parameters work on eight creator post lists: `instagram/profile/posts`, `instagram/profile/reels`, `tiktok/profile/videos`, `youtube/channel/videos`, `youtube/channel/shorts`, `facebook/profile/posts`, `twitter/user/tweets`, `threads/user/posts`, and per item on `POST /v1/prism/profiles` / `POST /v1/prism/jobs` with `include: "posts"`.

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/profile/posts?handle=nasa&stop_at_id=3990495229280545049"
```

- `stop_at_id` takes the `post.id` or `post.url` of the newest post you hold. The page stops just before it, no next cursor comes back, and the walk ends. If that post is not on this page, the page comes back whole with its cursor, so keep walking.
- `since` takes a date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, midnight UTC) or an ISO timestamp. Older posts are left off and the page that reaches one ends the walk. A post with no date is kept.
- Pinned posts sit out of date order at the top of a profile, so a pinned post never ends the walk.
- `pagination.stopped_at` reports why the walk stopped: `known_id`, `since`, `end` (the list ran out first) or `null` (keep walking). It is present only when you sent one of the two parameters.
- **Cost:** unchanged, the normal page price. A daily poll whose newest post is on page 1 pays for page 1 only. An unreadable date is a free 400.
- **YouTube:** either parameter forces newest-first order (`sort=popular` with either is a 400), and YouTube list dates are estimated from labels like "4 months ago", so prefer `stop_at_id` there.

`since` is also accepted on `search/multi`, `bluesky/search`, a few GitHub lists and some Prism composites; each endpoint's reference says what it does there.

## Search Filters and Multi-Page Walks

The platform keyword searches can filter rows, walk several pages in one call, and skip rows this account already received. A call that sends none of these parameters (or only `max_pages=1`) is unchanged.

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/search?query=skincare%20routine&min_views=500000&max_age_days=365&exclude_country=IN&max_pages=2"
```

| Param | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `min_views` | Keeps rows with at least that many `post.engagement.views`; a row with no view count is left off | TikTok keyword / top / hashtag search, Instagram reels and hashtag search, YouTube search / advanced / hashtag search, X tweet search |
| `max_age_days` | Keeps rows published within 1-3650 days; a row with no date is left off | The `min_views` searches plus `reddit/search` and `facebook/search/posts` |
| `country` / `exclude_country` | Up to 30 comma-separated codes, read from rows that carry a country. They filter rows; they do not move the search (that is `region`) | TikTok keyword and top search (and Instagram reels search via `country`, see its reference) |
| `sort_rows=views` | Orders the kept rows by views, highest first, across every page walked | The `min_views` searches |
| `max_pages` | 1-5 (default 1). Walks that many pages and returns the rows together | All of the above plus `threads/search` |
| `seen=<id>` | 1-64 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`. Rows this account already received under that id in the last 24 hours are left off | Same as `max_pages` |

- `data.walk` reports the pages walked, rows fetched and returned, `discarded` counts per reason (`views_below_min`, `older_than_max_age`, `country_excluded`, ...), `duplicates`, `repeats`, and `stopped` (`end`, `max_pages`, `time_budget`, `page_error`). `data.next_cursor` continues from the stop.
- **Cost:** each page walked costs one call to that endpoint (a cached page is free), and anything the endpoint already adds per page (`include`, `relevant_to`, `limit`) is added on each page. Filters do not reduce the price: rows a filter leaves off were still fetched. With `seen`, a page is billed `ceil(page price x new rows / rows on page)`, so a page of nothing but repeats costs 0 (refunded, shown in `data.walk.credits`). Quote `max_pages x page price` as the ceiling.
- A bad value (for example `max_pages=9`) is a free 400.

## Labels, Relevance and Quality

Many comment, post, review and search endpoints now judge each row. Each endpoint section in a platform reference lists `label`, `relevance` and the related params when the endpoint offers them.

**On by default, free.** Without asking, these run on every page and publish a score so you choose the cut-off:

- **Comment lists** (10 endpoints, e.g. `tiktok/post/comments`, `youtube/video/comments`, `reddit/post/comments`): `sentiment`, `question`, `purchase_intent`, `complaint`.
- **Post lists and keyword searches** (creator post lists, the TikTok / Instagram / YouTube / X / Reddit / Facebook / Hacker News / Threads / LinkedIn searches): `sponsored` (paid or gifted, disclosure, promoted account), `intent`, `niche` (one of 33).
- **Review lists** (22 endpoints across retail, app stores, Trustpilot, G2, Yelp, Tripadvisor, Google Business): `sentiment` read from the text, the main `issue`, and a flag when the words contradict the star rating.
- **Keyword searches** (and `search/everywhere`, `search/forums`, `search/creators`, `search/multi`): a `relevance` score on every row against your query. Nothing is dropped or reordered unless you ask.

Labels land on each row at `computed.labels.<preset>`, relevance at `computed.relevance`; `data.labels` and `data.relevance` report what ran on the page. A row that could not be judged in time ships with `null` and is filled on a later call or cached read. Every existing field, row and order is unchanged; `judgments=off` (or `label=none`) removes all of it.

**Opt-in** (CSV, alongside the defaults):

| Ask with | Adds | Price |
|---|---|---|
| `label=spam`, `label=toxic`, `label=low_quality` (comments) | Those labels; `exclude=spam` / `exclude=low_quality` drops them and lists `dropped_ids` | Metered |
| `label=quality` (posts) | `fact_density` 0-3, `engagement_bait`, `rage_bait`, `secondhand`, `post_aim`; `exclude=engagement_bait` drops bait | Metered |
| `label=injection` (comments, posts, reviews) | `{ flagged, p }` for text that tries to instruct an AI agent. Never drops or rewrites rows; not a security boundary | Metered |
| `label=mention&brand=<name>` (posts) | Whether the post is about your brand or a namesake, stance, aspect, and whether the author used it | Metered |
| `offer=<what you sell>` (with `intent`) | Whether it would help each author | Metered |
| `label=reports&reports=<phrase>` (reviews) | Whether each review reports that thing, in any wording | Metered |
| `relevance=filter` | Drops rows that use your keywords for something else and lists their ids | Free against your own query |
| `relevance=filter&relevant_to=<topic>` | The same, against a topic in your words (for ambiguous queries) | Metered |
| `label_evidence=1` (with `label=`) | The sentence that earned each label, copied from the text | Free |
| `dry_run=1` | `data.estimate`: `rows_expected`, `rows_cached`, `label_credits_min` / `max`, `base_credits`. Fetches nothing | Free (0 credits) |
| `fit=goal&goal=<task>` (optional `fit_tokens`) | Keeps the rows and fields needed for that goal (plus uncertain ones and the first and last block); the rest are stubbed and listed in `data.held_back` with a recall id | Free |

**Metered** means **+1 credit per 25 rows judged for the first time**, on top of the page. The router holds the ceiling up front (4 credits for a 100-row page; 5 on `tiktok/search`, 8 on `linkedin/search/posts` and `search/multi`) and refunds down to rows actually judged. A row already judged, a cached page, and a page where nothing could be judged add nothing. Use `dry_run=1` before a large labelled pull.

**Search judgments.** `search/everywhere` also returns each post's stance on your query, `data.stance_split` (counts per platform and overall, with the ids behind every count) and `data.topic_coverage` (`{ verdict: "ok" | "thin" | "none_relevant", best_p }`, beside the unchanged numeric `data.coverage`). `search/forums` fills `stance_split`; `search/news` groups articles about the same event into `data.stories`; `search/creators` labels each account as a creator, brand, media outlet or fan page (`brief=` ranks fits for +2 credits).

## Page-Level Shares and Signals

Free blocks on pages you already pull. They never drop or reorder rows.

- **`data.label_share`** (comment lists and `prism/comments`): for question, purchase intent, complaint and sentiment, how many comments were on the page, how many counted, how many were left out, a 90% interval, and up to three verbatim comments. A share whose interval is wider than 0.25 comes back `too_few: true` with no headline percentage; do not quote a percentage then. Removed by `judgments=off`.
- **`data.comment_language`** (comment lists): the commenters' language mix. Script-based languages are read from the script, others classified into a fixed list; unsure rows are counted in `abstained`, emoji-only or one-word replies are `cannot_tell`. A language is not a country. `GET /v1/prism/audience-language` does the same across a creator's recent posts.
- **`data.comment_recency`** (comment lists): share of the page posted in the last 24 hours and in the later half of the post's life, and a `stage` (`alive`, `slowing`, `spent`, `too_young`, `unknown`). Under eight dated comments gives no stage; on TikTok's own order the recent share is a floor (`recent_share_is_floor`).
- **`data.creator_baseline` + `computed.vs_creator`** (the eight creator post lists above): each post's views divided by the median of the creator's other comparable posts on the page (likes for Instagram photos and carousels). Pinned posts are excluded; a post under 48 hours is `too_young`; fewer than eight comparable posts gives `baseline: null` with reason `fewer_than_eight`.
- **`data.scan`** (`instagram/post/comments`, `tiktok/post/comments` with `scan_pages` up to 3, or TikTok `sort=recent`): reads several comment pages in one call, removes repeats and sorts in code. `data.scan.complete` says whether the whole thread was read. Each page that added comments is billed at the page price; the rest of the hold is refunded.

## Row Hydration (`include=`)

Many list endpoints return rows the upstream surface does not fully populate. A Pinterest search row carries no save count, a TikTok user-search row no bio or region, a YouTube playlist row no view count, a LinkedIn people row no exact follower count. Those leaves are `null` on a plain call.

**`include=` fills them in the same call.** It is an opt-in, CSV, enum-typed query param: each row is joined to a sibling endpoint on the same platform and only the leaves the row lacks are copied onto it. Nothing already on the row changes. A typo is a free pre-billing 400.

33 list endpoints across 8 platforms offer one. The tokens are `profile`, `engagement`, `details`, `channel`, `ad`, `saves`, `audio`, `creator` and `about`; which one an endpoint accepts, and exactly which leaves it fills, is in its endpoint section.

**How it is priced. Read this before sending one.** The join is charged per row, on top of the page:

- An **upfront ceiling** is held: `base + (credits per row x rows joinable)`.
- It is **refunded down to rows actually filled**. A row the sibling could not fill is refunded; a row served from the sibling's own cache is **free**.
- `credits_used` on the response is the real charge. A `data.hydration` block itemises rows, rows looked up, filled, cache hits, unfilled, credits held and kept (`extra_credits`), and milliseconds. On a `max_pages` walk it sums every page.

So `GET /v1/pinterest/search` is 1 credit plain and **up to 26** with `include=engagement`; `GET /v1/linkedin/search/people` is 10 plain and **up to 50** with `include=profile` (4 credits a row); `GET /v1/instagram/search/reels` is 1 plain and **up to 61** with `include=creator` (2 credits per creator looked up, 30 rows). Never quote the plain heading cost for a hydrated call.

Traps worth knowing:

- **`limit` caps rows and credits together** on the endpoints that offer it. `limit=5` on Pinterest search holds `1 + 5`, not `1 + 25`. Use it to bound spend.
- **`instagram/similar` defaults to its top 20 rows** when you send `include=profile` without `limit` (a hold of 25, not 85). `limit=80` buys the full roster at up to 85 credits. `instagram/search/profiles?include=about` likewise defaults to 8 rows (hold 17) at 2 credits a row.
- **On `threads/user/posts`, `threads/search` and the Facebook event, photo and post endpoints, `limit` is _not_ a row cap.** It switches the source or sets the walker's target, so those endpoints hold their full window regardless.
- **YouTube joins are batch-priced**: 1 credit per distinct id but never more than 5 per 50 ids, so a 50-row page adds 5, not 50. On a channel-scoped list (`channel/videos`, `channel/shorts`) the join is a single shared lookup: 1 credit.
- **Same-account check.** When a join's lookup answers with a different handle, the profile is copied only if it is still the same account (a rename). Otherwise the row keeps its own values, is not charged, and `data._warnings` names both handles (`resolved_to_different_handle`).

Latency: a hydrated page adds roughly 3-10 seconds on a fresh call (lookups run in parallel, bounded per row; Instagram `include=creator` 5-17 seconds) and nothing when the rows are already cached.

The per-endpoint ceilings are tabulated in [cost-gate.md](cost-gate.md#row-hydration-include). Always confirm against the endpoint's own **Pricing** line in its platform reference.

## Opt-In Enrichments on Single Endpoints

Each is off unless you send it and is documented in full in the platform reference named:

- **Transcript questions and moments** (`youtube/video/transcript`, `tiktok/post/transcript`; see [youtube.md](youtube.md), [tiktok.md](tiktok.md)): `q=<question up to 300 chars>` returns `data.moments` with `kind: "answers_query"`, start/end times and a quoted line for each stretch that answers it (`[]` when the video never does). `moments=brand,sponsor_read,product_demo,call_to_action` (optional `brand=`) returns timestamped moments instead. Send one or the other. Neither adds credits today.
- **Creator's own email** (`instagram/profile`, `youtube/channel`, `youtube/channel/about`): `contact_email=1` adds `author.ext.contact_email`, the address the creator gives for personal contact when the bio lists two or more; null when unclear or when every address is a manager's or agency's. `author.ext.public_email` is unchanged. No extra credits; any value other than `1` is a free 400.
- **Switch receipts** (`search/everywhere`, `reddit/search/comments`, `twitter/search/tweets`): `switch_from=<brand>` adds `data.switch_receipts`, the rows where the author personally left that brand, with the verbatim text, reason, destination and confidence. Counts only, never a percentage (`headline` is null). No extra credits.

## Account State and Not-Found Reasons

A profile or profile-list lookup that cannot return an account is `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` at 0 credits, with `error.details.reason`:

| Reason | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `account_gone` | The platform reports no account under this identifier: removed, deactivated, renamed, or never existed | On YouTube, retry once with `channelId` set to the `author.id` (`UC...`) you stored: a 200 means a rename (the new handle is in `author.username`); a second 404 means gone. `error.details.suggestion` says so |
| `account_private` | The account exists but does not serve this data publicly | On Instagram, `GET /v1/instagram/profile` still returns 200 with `author.private: true`, so keep the handle on a tracked list |
| `handle_unresolved` | No source could resolve it and none gave a reason | Check the handle; do not treat it as deleted |

`GET /v1/instagram/profile` also returns `author.last_post_at`, the newest post time on the profile page (pinned posts excluded), at no extra cost; null means unknown (private, or no posts readable). `prism/handle-audit` publishes the same reason per platform as `platforms.<platform>.evidence.profile.not_found_reason`.

## Chain Hints (`meta.hint`)

A response can name one other call that does the job in fewer steps, when this call just completed the pattern:

```json
"meta": { "hint": { "code": "search_multi", "method": "GET", "path": "/v1/search/multi?query=matcha&platforms=instagram,tiktok,youtube", "message": "..." } }
```

| Code | Pattern | Points to |
|---|---|---|
| `creator_card` | Same creator looked up on three platforms | `/v1/prism/creator-card` |
| `batch_profiles` | Many single profile lookups on one platform in half an hour | `POST /v1/prism/profiles` or `POST /v1/prism/jobs` |
| `search_multi` | Same query searched on three platforms | `/v1/search/multi` |
| `incremental_sync` | Page 1 of the same post list fetched again within a day | `stop_at_id` / `since` |
| `comment_labels` | A search, then comments on several of its posts without `label=` | The free `computed.labels` and `/v1/prism/comments` |
| `search_repeat` | Page 1 of the same search on an earlier visit | `seen=` or the endpoint's date filter |

When the suggested call costs more than the calls it replaces, `message` says both prices; follow the hint only if it fits the user's budget. Each code reaches a key at most once a day, never on an error or a replay, and the rest of the response is unchanged. `X-SocialCrawl-Hints: off` disables it.

## Planning and Self-Discovery (free)

All `/v1/utility/*` endpoints cost 0 credits. See [utility.md](utility.md).

- **`GET /v1/utility/plan?query=<the job in plain words>`** returns the calls to make, in order: each step's path, the params your words filled, the ones still missing, its credits, which earlier step feeds it (for example the post URL for comments), and a curl with placeholders such as `{handle}`. It plans brand watching, one creator's profile and posts, a search across platforms, and a scheduled search via a monitor; a single-call question returns that call plus close alternatives. Out-of-scope requests come back `uncertain: true` with `steps: []`, and things the API does not return are listed under `cannot`. It runs nothing. The parameter is `query`, not `q`.
- **`GET /v1/utility/endpoint?id=<platform/resource>`** is one endpoint's usage guide. When that endpoint was sampled in the rolling seven-day window it includes `quality`: `fill_rate` per field, `freshness_hours`, `sampled_calls`, `measured_from` / `measured_to`, and `null_by_design` for fields that are null on purpose. `measured: false` means no sample, not a perfect score.
- `GET /v1/utility/endpoints` (search the live registry), `/v1/utility/capabilities`, `/v1/utility/quickstart`, `/v1/utility/llms`.

## Raw Format

Add `?format=raw` to any endpoint whose response is normalized, to receive the original upstream body instead of the unified schema:

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/profile?handle=charlidamelio&format=raw"
```

What it changes and what it does not:

- **`data` becomes the upstream body verbatim.** No field map, no computed block, no `_warnings`, no `dropped`, and no envelope `pagination` block, because all of these describe the normalized payload. The upstream's own paging fields are in the raw body where the provider put them.
- **The envelope is unchanged.** `success`, `platform`, `endpoint`, `credits_used`, `credits_remaining`, `request_id` and `cached` are all still there, and the price is the same. Raw is a rendering choice, not a discount.
- **It shares the cache with the normalized call.** The response cache stores the raw upstream body and re-transforms on every read, so a raw request can be served from an entry a normalized request filled and vice versa. `format` is deliberately not part of the cache key: one entry, two renderings, no chance of the two disagreeing about what the provider said.
- **The 404-on-empty and refund rules still apply.** A nonexistent handle is still a 404 with the credit returned; raw does not turn an empty result into a 200.
- **It is a no-op where there is nothing to bypass.** Passthrough endpoints (GitHub, Tavily, Polymarket, Perplexity, Naver, Prism, Universal Search, Web, Utility, Content Analysis, twitter ai-search and the other research surfaces) already return the upstream shape, so the parameter changes nothing there.
- **An endpoint that owns the name wins.** A few endpoints take a real `format` parameter of their own (`youtube/transcripts`, `youtube/video/comments`, `youtube/video/comment/replies`, `youtube/video/subtitles`, `google/company/ads`, `utility/llms`, `tavily/extract`, `tavily/crawl`). On those, `format` means what their own docs say and `raw` is rejected by their validator. A few opt-ins (for example Instagram reels `include=creator`) cannot be combined with `format=raw`; that is a free 400.

## Field Projection

Add `?fields=` to keep only the fields you will use on each row. On a captured post page, a 4-field projection cut the rows by about 87%, so many more rows fit in a context window. The price is the same.

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/instagram/profile/posts?handle=nasa&fields=post.content.text,post.engagement.likes"

curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/post/comments?url=<video url>&fields=comment.text,comment.author.username,comment.engagement.likes"
```

- **Paths are comma-separated dot paths relative to one row:** an element of `data.items[]` on a list, `data` itself on a single object. Paths start with the row's root key, exactly as the endpoint's output fields are listed (`GET /v1/utility/endpoint?id=<platform/resource>`): `post.content.text`, `comment.author.username`, `author.followers`. `engagement.likes` without the root key matches nothing.
- **`*` matches any key at its segment.** `post.engagement.*` keeps every engagement count; `post.*.username` keeps `username` wherever it sits under `post`. A path that ends on an object keeps that whole object. Arrays are walked element by element (`post.media.url`).
- **Identity is always kept:** `id` and `url` at the row root and under the row's root key (`post.id`, `post.url`, `comment.id`), so a projected row can still be joined, deduplicated and cited.
- **Page-level keys are untouched:** `next_cursor`, `total`, `dropped`, `_warnings`, the report blocks and the envelope `pagination` block come back as usual. Pagination works the same.
- **An unknown path never fails the call.** The page is served and `data._warnings` gets a line such as `fields: 'post.content.txt' matched no field; did you mean 'post.content.text'?`. When `data` is a bare array the line goes in a `_warnings` list on the envelope instead. A path the endpoint does publish but that is empty on this page is not reported.
- **Never billed, one cache entry.** Projection runs on the finished response, after billing and the cache: a second call with different `fields` is a free cache hit. An `Idempotency-Key` retry must send the same `fields`.
- **Not applied with `format=raw`**, which returns the upstream body verbatim.
- **Row walks** (`min_views`, `max_age_days`, `seen` and the other walk filters, on the endpoints that offer them) filter on the full rows first, then project the merged page.
- **POST batch reads take `?fields=` in the query string** (the JSON body is unchanged). Each row of `data.results[]` is projected and its bookkeeping (`index`, `custom_id`, `target`, `status`, `cost`, `error`, `fetched_at`) is always kept:
  - `prism/profiles`: paths are relative to the row's `data`, as on the single profile endpoint: `fields=author.followers,author.username`.
  - `youtube/transcripts`: relative to the row's `data`: `fields=transcript,language`.
  - `prism/post-stats`: relative to the row: `fields=engagement.likes,engagement.views` (`url`, `id`, `shortcode` are always kept).
  - `prism/comment-lookup`: relative to the row: `fields=comment.text,comment.author.username`.
  - `youtube/videos`, `youtube/channels`: a normal list, as on GET: `fields=post.engagement.views`.
- **Not projected:** Server-Sent Event streams, `dry_run=1` cost previews, error bodies, `POST /v1/prism/jobs` results, and the stateful `/v1/web/*`, `/v1/monitors/*` and `/v1/cohorts/*` routes.

## Caching

Responses are cached by deterministic key (platform + resource + sorted query params; undeclared params are not part of the key). A cache hit costs 0 credits; each endpoint's **Cost** line gives its TTL in seconds. Cache category TTLs:

| Category | TTL |
|----------|-----|
| profile | 15 min |
| post | 10 min |
| comments | 5 min |
| search | 2 min |
| analytics | 30 min |
| immutable (single-video transcripts) | 30 days |

An endpoint can override its category TTL (some are never cached, for example live web scrapes and the Prism batch refreshes); each endpoint section in a platform reference states its own cache TTL.

- **Cache hits are free**: 0 credits, `X-Cache: HIT`, `cached: true`, `credits_remaining: null`.
- **Force a fresh fetch** with the request header `Cache-Control: no-cache`. It skips the lookup (billed as a normal miss) and writes the result back. Adding junk params does not bypass the cache.
- **A definitive not-found is remembered for one hour**, so a repeat lookup of a dead handle is a free 404.
- A cached empty body answers like the live path: `200 { items: [] }` for a list, `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` for a single object, both free.
- SSE streaming requests skip the cache entirely, both lookup and write.

## Idempotent Retries

Any charging `/v1/*` call can be made safely retryable by sending an `Idempotency-Key` header (UUIDv4 or any opaque 16+ char string):

| Outcome | HTTP | Credits | Notes |
|---------|------|---------|-------|
| First call | (normal) | cost | Reserved before billing; the completed response is stored for 24h |
| Replay (same key, same params) | Original status with stored body | 0 | `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`, body `idempotent_replay: true`, `credits_used: 0` |
| Payload mismatch (same key, different params) | 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` | 0 | Use a fresh key |
| Original request still running | 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` | 0 | Wait for `Retry-After: 1`, then retry the same key |
| Completed body exceeded 64 KB | 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE` | 0 | Use a new key only to make a new billable request |

Keys are scoped per account. An unfinished claim expires after 5 minutes; the claim store fails closed before billing (a `503` with `Retry-After: 1`) if it is unavailable. Requests without the header skip this subsystem. `POST /v1/prism/jobs` with a repeated key returns the existing job instead of a second one.

GET endpoints cannot combine `Idempotency-Key` with `Accept: text/event-stream`, because an interrupted stream has no complete response body to replay. Use `Accept: application/json` when you need idempotent replay. The unsupported combination returns an unbilled `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; POST batch streams retain their documented replay behavior.

## Rate and Concurrency Limits

Two separate limits, both per API key, both unbilled when they trip:

| Limit | Value | Code | Headers |
|-------|-------|------|---------|
| Requests per window | 600 per minute (sliding) | `429 RATE_LIMITED` | `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset`, `Retry-After` |
| Simultaneous in-flight | 50 concurrent | `429 CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` | `X-Concurrency-Limit` / `-Remaining`, `Retry-After` |

Honor `Retry-After`, then back off exponentially with jitter. The request-window limiter fails open, so a limiter outage never blocks traffic.

A JSON request body over **1 MB** is rejected with `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` before it is parsed. Split an oversized batch instead, or use `POST /v1/prism/jobs` for up to 5,000 items.

## Non-GET Routes, Streaming and Two-Step Endpoints

**Not everything is a GET.** Never assume the method: every endpoint section in a platform reference is headed by its real verb and carries a runnable curl. The non-GET routes are:

- **Batch reads** (`POST /v1/youtube/videos`, `/v1/youtube/channels`, `/v1/youtube/transcripts`, `/v1/prism/post-stats`, `/v1/prism/profiles`, `/v1/prism/comment-lookup`): the id/URL list is too large for a query string, so it travels in a JSON body as a real array.
- **Background jobs** (`POST /v1/prism/jobs`): up to 5,000 `prism/profiles` or `prism/post-stats` items; answers `202` with a `job_id`, poll `GET /v1/prism/jobs/{job_id}` (free).
- **Web jobs, monitors, and sessions** (`/v1/web/*`): POST to submit or create, GET to poll or list, PATCH to update, DELETE to cancel or close. `POST /v1/web/parse` is `multipart/form-data`, not JSON.
- **Monitors** (`/v1/monitors/*`): see [monitors.md](monitors.md).
- **Cohorts** (`/v1/cohorts/*`, `/v1/cohort-queries/*`): POST to create a cohort or submit a query, **PUT** to upload members (the only PUT in the API), GET to poll and read results, DELETE to cancel or purge. POST and PUT require an `Idempotency-Key` UUID header. See [cohorts.md](cohorts.md).

A POST/PATCH call needs both headers:

```
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/youtube/transcripts" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ids":["dQw4w9WgXcQ","9bZkp7q19f0"]}'
```

**Streaming:** a few endpoints (`/v1/search/everywhere`, `/v1/search/news`, `/v1/prism/comments`, `/v1/prism/profiles`, `/v1/prism/app-reviews`, `/v1/reddit/omni-search`, `/v1/youtube/transcripts`) emit Server-Sent Events when you send `Accept: text/event-stream`. Omit that header to get one JSON body instead. `/v1/prism/answers` always streams, and `/v1/prism/video-intel` streams when `include` contains `transcript`; each endpoint's reference section says which behaviour it has.

**Two-step endpoints:** some resources need an id from an earlier call. Google Shopping `product`/`reviews`/`sellers` need ids from `product-search`; Tripadvisor `reviews` needs `url_path` from `search`; Google `hotels/info` needs `hotel_identifier` from `hotels/search`; every `linkedin/company/*` sub-resource needs `company_id` from `linkedin/company`; `facebook/post/comment/replies` needs `feedback_id` + `expansion_token` from `facebook/post/comments`; Target `product`/`reviews` need a TCIN; `content_analysis/category-trends` needs a `category_code` from `content_analysis/categories`. Every endpoint's parameter descriptions name its prerequisite.

## Task-Polled Platforms (latency note)

Google Shopping, Trustpilot, Tripadvisor, Google Trends, Google Finance, Content Analysis, most Google Business resources, most Google Play / App Store resources, Pinterest `url-stats`, and Amazon `product` run on a task-queue upstream. The API hides this behind a normal synchronous call, but expect **~10 to 45 seconds** of latency on those endpoints. Plan timeouts accordingly (60s is safe).

Separately, the web crawl / batch-scrape / agent endpoints and Prism background jobs are **async by design**: they return a job id immediately, and you poll (`GET /v1/web/jobs/{job_id}`, `GET /v1/prism/jobs/{job_id}`) or supply a webhook.

## Universal and Multi-Platform Search

**`/v1/search/everywhere`**: flat **20 credits** per call. Fans out across up to 17 sources in parallel (reddit, twitter-ai-search, youtube, tiktok, instagram, hackernews, polymarket, github, threads, pinterest, perplexity, tavily, linkedin, rumble + tiktok/instagram/youtube hashtag siblings in hashtag mode), then plans, fuses, reranks (about half a second), enriches with top comments, and clusters the results. Every post carries its stance and relevance; see [Labels, Relevance and Quality](#labels-relevance-and-quality) for `stance_split`, `topic_coverage`, `relevance=filter` and `switch_from`.

Two response modes via the `Accept` header:

- `application/json` (default): standard envelope with the full ranked result set and fan-out transparency (`sources_called`, `sources_failed`, `sources_succeeded`, `sources_pruned`, `coverage`, `partial_failure`).
- `text/event-stream`: typed SSE chunks: `meta`, `source_started`, `items`, `source_failed`, `plan_refined`, `ranked_partial`, `ranked_final`, `comments_enriched`, `clusters`, `warning`, `done`, `error`.

Billing: if every source answered and none had a row, the call is `200` with `items: []` at 0 credits. If nothing came back and a source failed, it is a refunded error. If fewer than half the called sources succeeded, half the price is refunded (10 credits charged). Otherwise 20.

**`/v1/search/multi`**: one query sent to several platforms' own search endpoints in one call (`platforms=` from tiktok, instagram, youtube, reddit, threads, twitter, facebook, linkedin; default the first five). Each row is exactly what that platform's search returns, with `platform` added, grouped by platform, duplicate URLs removed. Per-platform filters pass through prefixed (`tiktok.region=US`, `reddit.sort=new`). Each platform costs its own page price (1 credit, LinkedIn 5) **only when it returned rows**; the rest of the hold is refunded. `data.sources` gives each platform's status, rows, cost and `next_cursor` (send it to that platform's own endpoint for page 2). Use `search/multi` for raw rows at per-platform prices; use `search/everywhere` for a planned, ranked, clustered answer.

## Prism Composites (`/v1/prism/*`)

Server-side composites that fan out to several detail endpoints and fold the legs into one unified payload behind the standard envelope. Every composite emits a `legs[]` transparency array (`{endpoint, status, credits_used, latency_ms, error}`). Cross-platform recipes live under `/v1/prism/*`; a few keep their platform's own path and carry a `family: "prism"` flag (`{tiktok,instagram,youtube,twitter,facebook,linkedin}/profile/full`, `reddit/omni-search`). Pricing is flat or metered per recipe; batch composites can reserve hundreds of credits, so price them with [cost-gate.md](cost-gate.md). Metered composites (e.g. `prism/comments`, `prism/ai-visibility`) deduct an upfront ceiling and refund to the actual work done. Streaming composites (`prism/comments`, `prism/profiles`, `prism/app-reviews`, `reddit/omni-search`) support `Accept: text/event-stream`; `prism/answers` always streams, and `prism/video-intel` streams when `include` contains `transcript`. Three composites are **POST** because their input is a list too large for a query string: `prism/post-stats`, `prism/profiles`, `prism/comment-lookup`.

`POST /v1/prism/profiles` with `"include": "posts"` (up to 25 items) also returns each found handle's first page of posts, at the profile price plus 1 credit per posts page that came back with posts; `since` and per-item `stop_at_id` work as on the single list endpoints.

**Background jobs.** `POST /v1/prism/jobs` with `{ "endpoint": "prism/profiles" | "prism/post-stats", "items": [...] }` takes up to 5,000 items, answers `202` with a `job_id` at once, and holds the whole price up front (each row priced as the batch endpoint prices it). It runs 50 items at a time. `GET /v1/prism/jobs/{job_id}` is free and shows progress, then the rows page by page; when it finishes you are charged for rows that came back and the rest is refunded. Add `webhook: { url }` for one signed completion message (the secret is in the first reply only). Full list and contracts: [prism.md](prism.md).

## Monitors (`/v1/monitors/*`)

A stateful, scheduled wrapper: a monitor re-runs any registered recipe or Prism composite on a cadence (hourly/daily/weekly/cron), delivers each result to an HMAC-signed webhook, evaluates alert rules, and accumulates a per-run time-series. Monitors are **not** registry endpoints (they sit outside the endpoint total) and use POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE. Managing them costs 0 credits; each scheduled run bills the recipe's normal cost plus a 1-credit scheduling premium. Full contract: [monitors.md](monitors.md).

## Platform Status

```bash
curl -s "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/status"
```

Returns per-platform circuit-breaker health. Each platform's breaker opens after 5 failures in 60s and stays open for 30s, during that window requests return `503` with `Retry-After: 30` and full refund.

## Error Codes

<!-- BEGIN:GENERATED:ERRORS (auto-generated by generate-docs.ts - AIP-16b) -->
| Code | Status | Retry? | What it means / what to do |
|------|--------|--------|----------------------------|
| MISSING_API_KEY | 401 | no | No x-api-key header on the request. Ask the user for their key and save it to `~/.config/socialcrawl/api_key` |
| INVALID_API_KEY | 401 | no | API key is malformed, not found, revoked, or expired. Tell the user to check the key at https://socialcrawl.dev/dashboard |
| INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS | 402 | no | Credit balance is lower than the endpoint cost. Point the user at https://socialcrawl.dev/dashboard/billing |
| INVALID_REQUEST | 400 | no | A required parameter is missing, a value failed validation, or no one-of group member was provided. Re-read the endpoint's params and Constraints in its platform reference before retrying - this is free, so a retry costs nothing |
| ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND | 404 | no | The platform or resource is not supported. Check references/index.md, or call the free `GET /v1/utility/endpoints` to list the live surface |
| RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND | 404 | no | The requested item was not found on the platform; credits are refunded when triggered by an empty upstream result |
| CONCURRENCY_LIMIT | 429 | yes | More than 50 simultaneous requests on the same API key; honor Retry-After, then back off. Wait for the `Retry-After` value, then retry |
| UPSTREAM_ERROR | 502 | yes | The platform returned an error; credits are automatically refunded. Retry once, then report it as a platform-side outage |
| SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE | 503 | yes | Temporarily unavailable for this platform, either after repeated failures or because the upstream provider is rate-limiting us; honor Retry-After, credits are refunded. Retry after ~30s |
| INTERNAL_ERROR | 500 | yes | Unexpected server error; credits are automatically refunded |
| METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED | 405 | no | Wrong HTTP method for this endpoint. Check the method in the platform reference - the `/v1/web/*` job, monitor, and session routes and the batch endpoints are POST/PATCH/DELETE, not GET |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT | 409 | no | The Idempotency-Key conflicts with an incompatible active reservation. Use a fresh Idempotency-Key |
| IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS | 409 | yes | A request with this Idempotency-Key is still running; retry after the Retry-After delay. Unbilled - wait for Retry-After, then retry with the same Idempotency-Key |
| IDEMPOTENCY_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE | 409 | no | The original outcome is known, but its response body exceeded the idempotent replay storage limit; use a new key only to make a new billable request. The prior call already completed; use a new key only to make a new billable request |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH | 422 | no | The Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request payload. Use a fresh Idempotency-Key for the changed payload |
| COHORT_MEMBER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED | 400 | no | The cohort member limit would be exceeded by this upload |
| COHORT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED | 400 | no | The account already holds the maximum number of cohorts |
| COHORT_IDENTITY_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED | 400 | no | The identity platform is not supported for cohort queries |
| COHORT_IDENTITY_CONFLICT | 409 | no | The normalized identity is already assigned to another external ID |
| COHORT_QUERY_NOT_CANCELLABLE | 409 | no | The cohort query is terminal and cannot be cancelled |
| COHORT_QUERY_NOT_READY | 409 | no | The cohort query has not completed and its results are not available |
| COHORT_RESULT_TOO_LARGE | 413 | no | One cohort query result exceeds the maximum response-page size |
| PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | 413 | no | The JSON request body exceeds the 1 MB size limit |
| RATE_LIMITED | 429 | yes | More than 600 requests in a 1-minute window on the same API key; honor Retry-After, then back off. Unbilled - wait for `Retry-After`, then retry |
| KEY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED | 402 | no | This API key has spent its per-key credit limit; the account balance is unaffected. Raise or reset the key's limit in Dashboard → API Keys, or use a key with no limit |
<!-- END:GENERATED:ERRORS -->

Error envelopes include a `doc_url` anchored on the errors page, `https://www.socialcrawl.dev/docs/errors#<code-slug>` (for example `#insufficient-credits`). `UPSTREAM_ERROR` can also arrive with HTTP status **504** when the source timed out; it is refunded and retryable like the 502.

## Error Details (`error.details`)

Branch on `error.details.reason` when present. Every case below is free (nothing charged or fully refunded).

| Status | `reason` / field | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `page_limit` (+ `max_page`, `requested_page`, `narrow_with`) | The page is past the source's last page for this query (e.g. Instagram reels search stops at page 11 with `date_posted`) | Stop paging; narrow with the params in `narrow_with` |
| 400 | `unsupported_geo_filter` (+ `unknown_parameters`) | A country filter this list cannot apply | Drop it or use an endpoint that filters by country |
| 400 | `suggestions` / `did_you_mean` (+ `unknown_parameters`) | A parameter name was one edit from a real one, or a detail endpoint needs `url` not an id | Fix the name and resend |
| 402 | `balance_too_low` (+ `retry_will_succeed: false`, `next_step`, `top_up_url`, `credits_required`) | Not enough credits | Do not retry. Tell the user to top up |
| 402 | `key_budget_reached` (+ `key_settings_url`) | This key hit its own credit limit; the account balance is fine | Do not retry. Raise the key's limit or use another key |
| 402 | `pricing: "ceiling"` (+ `lower_cost_with`) | The quoted credits are the most this call can cost (metered hold) | A smaller request (the listed params, e.g. `limit`) holds less |
| 404 | `account_gone` / `account_private` / `handle_unresolved` (+ `suggestion`) | See [Account State](#account-state-and-not-found-reasons) | Follow `suggestion` once; do not loop |
| 404 | `site_not_supported` (+ `retry_will_succeed: false`, `suggestion`) | `web/scrape` cannot read this site | Do not retry. For a social link, `suggestion` names the SocialCrawl endpoint that reads it |
